To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) hate-speech detection is a difficult task and 2) hate speech is more prevalent in tweets with explicit hate keywords.

(1) we developed a new dataset of tweets containing offensive language and hate speech; (2) we used this dataset to train a multi-class supervised classifier; (3) our classifier is able to distinguish between hate speech and offensive language with 85% accuracy; (4) our classifier is more accurate at classifying racist and homophobic tweets; (5) tweets without hate keywords are difficult to classify; and (6) we provide a detailed error analysis that shows when our classifier makes mistakes and
the majority of the tweets in the dataset are classified correctly by our classifier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how we can distinguish between offensive language and hate speech.
the problem of distinguishing hate speech from other types of offensive language.
the problem of automatically distinguishing between offensive language and hate speech in tweets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hate speech can be reliably detected in tweets containing hate keywords and that it is possible to separate hate speech from offensive language in tweets containing offensive keywords.
the classification of hate speech is more challenging than that of general offensive language and that the distinction between the two is not always clear.
hate speech is a very small fraction of offensive language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hate speech can be detected with a good precision, but the detection of offensive language in general is a much harder task.
the use of hate speech keywords is not a reliable indicator of hate speech.

we have developed a classifier that can distinguish between hate speech and offensive language and that this classifier can be used to help identify tweets containing offensive language but not hate speech.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to distinguish between hate speech and other forms of offensive language on social media.
hate speech detection is a more complex problem than previously thought.
hate speech is not a binary concept but rather a spectrum.
